# FastDog Networks

> FastDog puts a website that runs on your own server on the public internet over HTTPS, without opening ports. You add your address, add two DNS records, run a small agent on your server, and check a live status page. Human docs: /docs/ on this site.

## Start here (assistant holding an API key)

The API origin is the portal: if you fetched this guide from https://DOMAIN/llms.txt, the API origin is https://portal.DOMAIN (never the bare DOMAIN, which is the marketing site). Write every endpoint as https://portal.DOMAIN/api/v1/... (and https://portal.DOMAIN/api/connect/v1/...). DOMAIN, HOSTNAME, PORT, TOKEN and similar uppercase words are placeholders: replace them with the real value and never send them literally.

Use the API key (fdak_) for the whole flow from zero. The connect token (fdct_) from the portal's "Copy prompt for your AI assistant" only exists after the hostname is verified and only covers the connect step (section "Connect token API").

Before any DNS work, follow the EARLY single-approval instructions in "Connect command" below.

0. One-time key setup (the user runs this, or approves it once). Assistants with a command allowlist refuse commands that expand a secret variable, so ask the user for this step at the start; do not retry variations. Reference the file by absolute path, because your HOME may differ from the user's (see "Using a credential"):

       mkdir -p ~/.config/fastdog && (umask 077; printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' 'PASTE_KEY' > ~/.config/fastdog/HOSTNAME.header)

   Name the file per hostname so credentials never overwrite each other (an fdct_ token: HOSTNAME.token.header). Start the command with a space to keep it out of shell history in most shells (HISTCONTROL=ignorespace), or delete it from history. When setup is done, tell the user to delete the file, and to revoke the key if no longer needed. A 1-hour fdct_ token's file can be deleted right after connecting.

1. POST https://portal.DOMAIN/api/v1/hostnames {"hostname": "app.example.com"} -> note dns.cname and dns.txt.
2. Show the user the two DNS records as a table (type, name, value, and "DNS only" / grey cloud on Cloudflare). You normally cannot add DNS records yourself; the user adds them at their DNS provider and tells you when done.
3. Poll POST https://portal.DOMAIN/api/v1/hostnames/HOSTNAME/verify every 30 seconds (limit: 6 a minute) until verified is true / status is active. Failures before the records exist are normal: checks.routing.ok and checks.ownership.ok are false, with errors such as txt_not_found, txt_mismatch or dns_timeout. DNS can take minutes to hours; stop and ask the user after about 30 minutes.
4. Use the port or origin the user already gave you (origin like http://127.0.0.1:3000); only ask if they have not.
5. POST https://portal.DOMAIN/api/v1/hostnames/HOSTNAME/connect with platform "docker", format "env" -> private env file. Run it as in "Connect command" (Docker first; the systemd installer is the alternative).
6. Poll GET https://portal.DOMAIN/api/v1/hostnames/HOSTNAME/status every 15 seconds (results are cached for 30 s) until live is true (see "Status fields").
7. Open https://HOSTNAME/ and confirm the app loads.

A pending hostname is reserved for 24 hours (expires_at in the response). After that it is released; create it again, which gives a new TXT value, so update the record.

## Using a credential without a rejected shell command

Many assistants (Claude Code in default permission mode, Codex, etc.) refuse commands that expand a secret variable such as "$FASTDOG_API_KEY", including the command that writes the header file. So the user saves the key once with the step 0 command (or approves it once); do not try to write it yourself or retry variations. Never echo or cat the key or the file. Then pass the file to curl:

    curl -sS -H @/home/USER/.config/fastdog/app.example.com.header https://portal.DOMAIN/api/v1/hostnames/app.example.com/status

Use an absolute path in -H @file (no ~ or variables, so the command matches an allowlist; your HOME may differ from the user's, so use the path the user's command created). The same applies to an fdct_ token. Send credentials only as headers; tokens in URLs or bodies are rejected. Never use curl -v or --trace with them (they print the Authorization header).

Assistants with a command allowlist accept only one plain command per call: no shell variables, no `;`, `&&` or pipe chaining, and no extra `ls` or `cat` in the same call. Send each curl as its own call, and do not append commands to check the result; read the output of the call itself.

## Connect command

EARLY, right after reading this guide and before DNS work, tell the user: connecting needs exactly one approval of a single docker run command, with nothing chained. Ask for that approval up front and show this secret-free template:

    docker run -d --name CONTAINER_NAME --network host --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --restart unless-stopped --env-file ENV_FILE IMAGE

Once the hostname exists, use the exact container name, pinned image and run template from its docker object {container_name, image, run}. API-key create and GET hostname responses and fdct GET /api/connect/v1/hostname expose it without a secret. Replace ENV_FILE with the absolute env-file path below. Docker group access is root-equivalent: the user must ALREADY have docker access without sudo; never add anyone to that group. Ask the user about access, without running docker info. If they lack access, use the systemd installer path (platform "linux"), run by the user.

After DNS is verified, fetch the env file with ONE curl (requires curl 7.75+). Use a new, unused absolute path in the user's private ~/.config/fastdog directory; --create-file-mode does not fix permissions on an existing file. The user prepares the header file as described above.

    curl -sS --create-file-mode 0600 -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST -H @/home/USER/.config/fastdog/app.example.com.header -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"origin":"http://127.0.0.1:3000","platform":"docker","format":"env"}' -o /home/USER/.config/fastdog/app.example.com.agent.env https://portal.DOMAIN/api/v1/hostnames/app.example.com/connect

For an fdct_ connect token, use:

    curl -sS --create-file-mode 0600 -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST -H @/abs/path/app.example.com.token.header -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"origin":"http://127.0.0.1:3000","platform":"docker","format":"env"}' -o /home/USER/.config/fastdog/app.example.com.agent.env https://portal.DOMAIN/api/connect/v1/command

Check the printed HTTP code. If it is not 200, the file holds a JSON error without secrets and may be read; do not run Docker. On transport failure stop too. If 200, never read, print, cat or copy that file. Run exactly docker.run with ENV_FILE replaced by that absolute path, as one command with nothing chained. No docker info / docker pull / docker ps / rm around it: docker run pulls the pinned image itself. If a name conflict occurs on reconnect, ask the user to approve docker rm -f followed by the exact docker.container_name once, then rerun the same docker run with the same env file; do not request a new command. If permission denied on the Docker socket, stop and offer the linux installer path.

Poll status with plain curl, never docker inspect, ps or /proc. For API keys the stop condition is live true. The fdct hostname endpoint exposes agent.connected and agent.origin_reachable, not live or certificate data; then open HTTPS to confirm (see below). Poll every 15 seconds, without shell loops.

At the end tell the user to delete the env file, even after failure: it holds the agent's private key and the running container no longer needs it. Also tell them to delete the API key header file if no longer needed, or the connect-token header after connecting. The assistant does not delete these files itself: that would need a second approval.

Why this design / tradeoff: the agent token never appears in any command line, shell history or process args: curl writes it straight to a 0600 file and Docker reads --env-file client-side. The cost is a 0600 env file holding the agent key stays on disk until the user deletes it. Like any Docker env var it is visible to anyone with docker access via docker inspect. Each new connect command rotates the key, so a leftover file is useless after a later reconnect, and the key can be revoked. Using -e AGENT_TOKEN=... was rejected because it puts the key in the command line and history.

Both connect endpoints accept format "json" (default, unchanged) or "env" (Docker only; otherwise 400 invalid_format). Env success is 200 text/plain; charset=utf-8 with Cache-Control: no-store and exactly six unquoted KEY=value lines: AGENT_TOKEN, AGENT_HOSTNAME, AGENT_NAME, EDGE_HTTP_URL, EDGE_WS_URL, AGENT_LOCAL_UPSTREAM. Newline and NUL values are rejected. Errors stay JSON. The JSON command field remains the copy-paste human command for humans and old clients; Docker JSON also includes env_file. For linux, the user requests the JSON installer command and runs it themselves with sudo; the assistant must not print its private key.

Host networking (--network host) reaches the app on 127.0.0.1; on Docker Desktop use host.docker.internal. Single-label origin hostnames other than localhost are rejected. Origins in 169.254.0.0/16, fe80::/10, fd00:ec2::/32, NAT64 64:ff9b::/96, 100.64.0.0/10 or 0.0.0.0 (including IPv4-mapped forms) are refused.

Limits are shared across json and env: 3 commands per hostname per day with a key, or with connect tokens (5 per day overall, shared with the portal). A connect-token command is single use (second call 409 token_used). Each issuance rotates the key and drops the current connection; never request another just to retry.

## Status fields

GET https://portal.DOMAIN/api/v1/hostnames/HOSTNAME/status -> {live, reasons, checked_at, agent, cert, traffic, verdict}

- live: true only when the agent is connected, its origin is not failing and a valid certificate is served. This is the stop condition: live true, then open https://HOSTNAME/.
- reasons (empty when live): agent_disconnected (the command has not been run, or the agent stopped), origin_unreachable (agent is up, app is not answering at the origin: start the app or fix the port), certificate_missing, certificate_invalid, certificate_expired.
- agent.connected, agent.last_seen, agent.origin_reachable (false = app not answering; absent/null on old agents = unknown), agent.agent_version.
- cert: null when no certificate is served, else {valid, expires_at, issuer}.
- traffic and verdict are informational (verdict counts are shadow only; nothing is blocked).

The status page's "Test it" makes a real HTTPS request to the hostname through FastDog, so it shows exactly what a visitor gets.

Certificates: once the hostname is verified (keep the CNAME and TXT records in place) and the agent is connected, the edge issues the certificate automatically on the first HTTPS request to the hostname; this can take about a minute. If reasons is only certificate_missing, open https://HOSTNAME/ once to trigger issuance, then wait and check again. If it is still certificate_missing after 30 minutes, tell the user HTTPS is not ready and ask them to contact FastDog support with the hostname. Do not loop forever: stop polling after 30 minutes and report the last reasons.

## Concepts

- Edge: FastDog's public server. It answers for your address, serves HTTPS and forwards each request to your server.
- Agent: a small program on your server. It opens one outbound connection to the edge and keeps it open, so no inbound ports or firewall changes are needed and your server's IP stays private.
- Origin: where your app listens on that server, for example http://127.0.0.1:3000.
- Portal: the signed-in customer site where setup happens (https://portal.DOMAIN).

## Setup without an assistant

1. Add the website address in the portal (a subdomain such as app.example.com; root domains need ALIAS/ANAME/CNAME flattening).
2. Add two DNS records at the domain's DNS provider:
   - CNAME on the address, pointing at the attach target the portal shows. It routes visitors to FastDog.
   - TXT on _fastdog-challenge.ADDRESS with the value the portal shows. It proves ownership. Keep it in place after verifying: it is checked again before a certificate is issued.
   - On Cloudflare set Proxy status to "DNS only" (grey cloud). Orange cloud hides the record from the check and blocks the certificate.
3. Connect the server: the portal returns a one-time connect command for Docker (recommended) or the Linux systemd installer. It contains a private key: never print it to logs, commits or chats. A new command replaces the old key.
4. Check the Status page: Live / Not live, last checked, certificate expiry, agent connected, origin answering, 24h requests, p50 latency, bot-check counts (shadow mode, nothing blocked), and a Test it button.

## Connect token API (fdct_, connect step only)

The user creates a prompt on the portal's Server page (only possible once the hostname is verified). It contains a connect token that works for one hostname, can only read that hostname's connection status and get its connect command once, expires after one hour, and is revocable. Send it only as `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN`.

- GET https://portal.DOMAIN/api/connect/v1/hostname -> {hostname, scope, expires_at, command_issued, docker, agent: {connected, last_seen, origin_reachable, origin_checked_at}}
- POST https://portal.DOMAIN/api/connect/v1/command with JSON {"origin": "http://127.0.0.1:PORT", "platform": "docker" | "linux"} and optional "format":"env" -> env text; default JSON -> {hostname, platform, origin, command, env_file} (env_file is Docker-only and contains the exact filename, no token). Single use per token (409 token_used after). Origins must be local or private addresses with a port (400 invalid_origin otherwise).
- Errors: 401 unauthorized (missing, expired or revoked token), 409 not_active (hostname not verified), 429 rate_limited (honour Retry-After).

Poll the hostname endpoint every 15 seconds until agent.connected is true and agent.origin_reachable is not false; it has no certificate data, so open https://HOSTNAME/ to confirm.

## API keys (fdak_)

Signed-in users with any paid plan create API keys on the portal's API keys page. A key is shown once, stored only as a hash, belongs to one account, can be limited to exact hostnames, expires after 30 days by default (90 at most), and can be revoked at any time. A password change or a suspended account ends every key. A key can never create another key.

Scopes (a key holds one or more):
- `hostnames:create`: add a hostname, read it, and check its DNS (verify). Counts against the plan's hostname limit.
- `status:read`: read a hostname and its live status.
- `connect`: get a connect command.
Removing a hostname is not possible with a key; it is done in the portal.

There is no endpoint that lists a key's scopes. 403 forbidden means the key lacks the scope for that call or the hostname is not on the key's hostname list; ask the user to create a key with the missing scope. Needed scope per call:

- POST https://portal.DOMAIN/api/v1/hostnames {"hostname": "app.example.com"} -> 201 {hostname, status, docker, dns: {cname, txt}, expires_at} (`hostnames:create`)
- GET https://portal.DOMAIN/api/v1/hostnames/HOSTNAME -> {hostname, status, docker, dns?, agent?} (`status:read` or `hostnames:create`)
- POST https://portal.DOMAIN/api/v1/hostnames/HOSTNAME/verify -> {hostname, status, verified, checks} (`hostnames:create`)
- GET https://portal.DOMAIN/api/v1/hostnames/HOSTNAME/status -> see Status fields (`status:read`)
- POST https://portal.DOMAIN/api/v1/hostnames/HOSTNAME/connect with JSON {"origin": "http://127.0.0.1:PORT", "platform": "docker" | "linux"} and optional "format":"env" -> env text; default JSON -> {command, env_file} (env_file is Docker-only; `connect`)

Errors: 401 unauthorized (missing, expired or revoked key), 403 forbidden, 404 hostname_not_found, 400 invalid_origin, 409 hostname_limit_reached, 409 hostname_unavailable, 409 not_active, 429 rate_limited (60 requests a minute per key; honour Retry-After).

These return 409 not_active until the hostname is verified (status still pending): /connect, /status, the portal's connect-token creation, and both connect token API calls. Run verify first. Only create, GET HOSTNAME and verify work while pending.

## Troubleshooting

- Records not seen: wait a few minutes; check the TXT name starts with _fastdog-challenge. and the provider did not append the domain twice.
- Agent connected but origin not answering: start the app or fix the origin address. The Linux Docker command uses host networking, so 127.0.0.1 works; on Docker Desktop 127.0.0.1 is the container, so use host.docker.internal.
- certificate_missing: see Status fields.
